title: 第9章 往事如烟第10章 暗涌
content_zh:
山涧边有一块大石头。
石头很平，平得像一张床，又宽又长，能并排坐两个人。石头下面是溪水，溪水很清，清得能看见水底的沙和石子。石子上长着一层薄薄的青苔，被水流冲得一飘一飘的，像是有人在底下扯布条。
他们每天都在那里坐。
不是约好的，只是习惯。
第一次是巧合——他巡营路过山涧，看见她坐在石头上发呆，就在旁边坐下了。两人坐着，谁也没说话。坐到天黑，他站起来走了，她也站起来走了。走的时候，她往左，他往右。
第二次还是巧合——他来看溪水涨了没有，她已经在了。他在她旁边坐下，两人看着溪水流，流了很久，谁也没开口。
第三次就不是巧合了。
第三次他来的时候，石头上空空的。他站在那里，看了一会儿空石头，然后坐下来。坐了大约一盏茶的功夫，身后传来脚步声。很轻的脚步声，他不用回头就知道是谁。
她在旁边坐下。
两人谁也没提“你又来了“之类的话。
就这么坐着。
从那以后，每天早上或者傍晚——有时候是早上，有时候是傍晚，看谁先到——他们就在那块石头上坐一会儿。坐多久不一定。有时候坐一炷香，有时候坐到天黑。坐着的时候很少说话。他本来话就少，她也不是多话的人。两个不爱说话的人坐在一起，你不问我，我不答你，反而自在。
溪水在流。
流得慢，但一直在流。
这一天，她忽然开口了。
“你想听吗？“
肖琪转过头，看着她。
她坐在石头上，抱着膝盖，看着溪水。溪水在流，流过石头，流过水草，流进远处的树林里。风从溪面上吹过来，带着一种凉丝丝的水汽，吹得她额前的碎发轻轻晃。
“听什么？“他问。
“我的事。“

他看着她，盯了几息。
她的眼睛没有看他。她看着溪水，看着溪水在石头上撞出白色的水花，看着水花落下去，又溅起来，反反复复，永不停歇。
他转过头，也看向溪水。
“想说就说。“
和上次一样，四个字。
简短，干脆，像是在说一件很普通的事。
但和上次不一样的是，他说这四个字的时候，把手里正在削的一根木枝放下了。
他放得很轻，轻得几乎没有声音。
但她听见了。
她说她家在很远的地方。
远到她自己也记不清了。只记得那个地方冬天很冷，冷得河面结冰，冰厚得能在上面走人。夏天又很热，热得蝉叫一整个白天不停。院子很大，比这个营地还大。院子里有一棵桂花树，树龄比她爹还大，每年八月，桂花开了，满院子都是香味。那种香味很甜，甜得齁人，但她娘喜欢。她娘每年都会把桂花收起来，晒干了做桂花糕。
“我爹喜欢吃桂花糕。“她说，“但他嘴笨，从不说好吃。他就坐树下喝酒，喝到高兴了就唱歌。唱得很难听，我娘每次都捂耳朵。“
她笑了一下。
那个笑很浅，浅得像水面上一圈涟漪，漾开来就没了。
“后来呢？“肖琪问。
她没有回答。
她只是看着溪水，看了很久。
溪水在流，流得很慢，流过石头，流过水草，流进远处的树林里。
“我十二岁那年。“她忽然开口。
声音变了。

不是变大了，也不是变小了，是变了一种质地。像是溪水底下突然冒出来的一块石头，硬的，冷的，硌在声音里面。
“那天晚上来了很多人。“
她说。
“穿着黑衣服，手里拿着刀。很多刀。我听见了——先是敲门声，然后是我爹的声音，他在跟人说话，说得很急。然后我娘跑过来，把我推进地窖里。“
content_en:
There is a big stone beside the mountain stream.
The stone is very flat, as flat as a bed, wide and long, and can accommodate two people sitting side by side. Under the stone is a stream. The stream is very clear, so clear that you can see the sand and stones at the bottom. There was a thin layer of moss growing on the stones, which was washed away by the current, as if someone was pulling strips of cloth underneath.
They sit there every day.
It's not an appointment, it's just habit.
The first time was a coincidence - he passed by a mountain stream while patrolling the camp and saw her sitting on a stone in a daze, so he sat down next to her. The two of them sat without speaking. They sat there until it got dark, then he stood up and left, and so did she. When walking, she goes to the left and he goes to the right.
The second time was a coincidence - he came to see if the water in the stream had risen, and she was already there. He sat down next to her, and the two of them watched the stream flow for a long time without anyone speaking.
The third time was no coincidence.
When he came the third time, the stone was empty. He stood there for a moment looking at the empty stone, then sat down. After sitting for about a cup of tea, footsteps came from behind. There were very light footsteps, and he knew who it was without looking back.
She sat down next to him.
Neither of them said anything like "You're here again."
Just sit there.
From then on, every morning or evening - sometimes morning, sometimes evening, whichever came first - they sat on that stone for a while. It doesn't matter how long you sit. Sometimes I sit with a stick of incense, sometimes I sit until dark. He rarely talks while sitting. He doesn't talk much, and she isn't a talkative person either. Two people who don't like to talk sit together. You don't ask me and I don't answer you, but they feel comfortable.
The stream is flowing.
It flows slowly, but keeps flowing.
On this day, she suddenly spoke.
"Do you want to hear it?"
Xiao Qi turned her head and looked at her.
She sat on the stone, hugging her knees and looking at the stream. The stream is flowing, flowing through stones, water plants, and into the woods in the distance. The wind blew over the stream, bringing with it a cool vapor, causing the broken hair on her forehead to sway gently.
"Listen to what?" he asked.
"My business."
He looked at her for a few seconds.
Her eyes were not on his. She looked at the stream, watching the water hit white splashes on the rocks, watching the splashes fall and splash again, over and over again, never stopping.
He turned his head and looked towards the stream.
“Say what you want to say.”
Just like last time, four words.
It was short and concise, as if it was talking about a very ordinary thing.
But what was different from last time was that when he said these four words, he put down a branch he was whittling.
He let it go so gently that there was almost no sound.
But she heard it.
She said her home was far away.
It was so far away that she couldn't even remember it. I just remember that it was very cold in winter in that place, so cold that the river froze, and the ice was so thick that people could walk on it. It's very hot in summer, so hot that cicadas keep chirping all day long. The yard is huge, bigger than this camp. There is an osmanthus tree in the yard, which is older than her father. Every August, the osmanthus blossoms and the yard is filled with fragrance. The scent was very sweet, overpoweringly sweet, but her mother liked it. Her mother would collect the sweet-scented osmanthus every year and dry it in the sun to make sweet-scented osmanthus cake.
"My father likes to eat sweet-scented osmanthus cake," she said, "but he is stupid and never says it is delicious. He just sits under a tree and drinks, and when he is happy, he sings. The singing is very unpleasant, and my mother covers her ears every time."
She smiled.
That smile was very shallow, as shallow as a ripple on the water, and disappeared after it spread.
"What happened next?" Xiao Qi asked.
She didn't answer.
She just looked at the stream for a long time.
The stream is flowing, flowing very slowly, flowing through stones, flowing through water plants, and flowing into the woods in the distance.
"When I was twelve years old." She suddenly said.
The voice changed.
It’s not getting bigger or smaller, it’s just changing its texture. It was like a stone suddenly emerging from the bottom of the stream. It was hard and cold and struck the sound."A lot of people came that night."
she said.
"Wearing black clothes, they had knives in their hands. Lots of knives. I heard it - first the knock on the door, and then my dad's voice, talking to someone, very hurriedly. Then my mom came running over and pushed me into the cellar."
